raw:
These ten hypotheses come from contrasting parents within each edit's 100-experiment block. Most rest on only a handful of parents, so they are weak evidence. Hypotheses 1-2 and 3-4 are the best supported, with large effects consistent across all three datasets.

1. Edge 0 → nor_conv_3x3 gains much more when edge 3 is skip_connect (rows 2 and 5, +12 on C100 and IN16) than when edge 3 is a convolution (rows 3 and 4, +3.4 to +8.5).
2. The same edit gains more when edge 5 is avg_pool_3x3 or skip_connect (rows 7 and 9, +15 on C100) than when edge 5 is a convolution (rows 3 and 8, about +4.4).
3. Edge 4 → avg_pool_3x3 hurts much more when edge 3 is skip_connect (row 46, -11.7 on C100) than when edge 3 is nor_conv_3x3 or nor_conv_1x1 (rows 41 and 47, about -2 to -3).
4. The same edit also hurts more when edge 3 is none (row 45, -9.7 on IN16).
5. Edge 3 → skip_connect is worse when edge 5 is skip_connect (rows 11-15, mostly negative) than when edge 5 is a convolution (rows 17-19, positive).
6. Edge 5 → none costs less when edge 4 is nor_conv_3x3 (rows 81, 83-87, about -1 to -3 on C100) than when edge 4 is none, skip_connect or avg_pool_3x3 (rows 88-90, about -6 to -7).
7. Edge 1 → none hurts more when edge 2 is none (row 55, -9.4 on IN16), because edge 1 is then the only route into node 1's output paths.
8. Edge 2 → nor_conv_1x1 helps more when edge 1 is avg_pool_3x3 (rows 36-39, positive on all three datasets) than when edge 1 is a convolution (rows 34 and 35, smaller on C100).
9. Edge 3 → nor_conv_3x3 helps more when edge 3 was none (row 62, +6.1 on IN16), since it adds a connection rather than swapping an existing one.
10. Edge 2 → skip_connect is less harmful when edge 2 was avg_pool_3x3 (row 94, +0.7 on C100 and +1.0 on IN16) than when it was a convolution (rows 91 and 93, negative on both).
